# MM-P3-L4-SB03 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3
Revision: Rev C
Plant: P3, line P3-L4
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-SB03

Scope
- This document defines the preventive maintenance tasks, method, and acceptance criteria for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) in plant P3, line P3-L4.
- Tasks cover inspection, cleaning, wear measurement, media management, and fastener torque verification required to maintain safe and consistent blasting performance.
- This manual applies to maintenance technicians and process engineers responsible for EQ-P3-L4-SB03. Reference related documents for complementary procedures: SB-1019, SB-1038, SOP-P3-L4-02.

Background and rationale
- EQ-P3-L4-SB03 is a blast cabinet used after heat treat operations to remove scale and residue prior to downstream handling. Consistent blast energy, media condition, and wheel integrity are critical to part quality and process repeatability.
- The blast wheel liner secures the wheel assembly and maintains alignment. Fastener preload affects wheel vibration and media trajectory; improper torque leads to accelerated wear or unsafe operation. Therefore, verification of the blast wheel liner bolt torque is required.
- Shot media degrades and fines accumulate during operation. Topping up media maintains charge level and abrasive characteristics; regular intervals prevent process drift and reduce the need for corrective interventions during production.

Tools
- Calibrated torque wrench capable of reading and applying 90 N·m.
- Hand tools and socket set suitable for cabinet fasteners.
- Personal protective equipment: hearing protection, eye protection, respirator per SOP-P3-L4-02, gloves.
- Shop vacuum and non-sparking hand brush.
- Media handling container and funnel for controlled top-up.
- Inspection mirror and flashlight.
- Maintenance logbook or electronic maintenance record entry device.

Procedure
Preparation
- Lockout/tagout the isolation defined in SOP-P3-L4-02 for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 before any work. Verify energy sources are isolated per SOP-P3-L4-02 prior to opening access panels.
- Don required PPE before entry into the work area.

Inspection and cleaning
- Open the access panel to the blast wheel housing following the sequence in SB-1019 for safe access. Visually inspect the wheel, liner, and surrounding structure for cracks, unusual wear, or foreign objects.
- Remove accumulated dust and media fines from the housing and inlet areas using a shop vacuum and brush. Collect vacuumed material in the provided container for disposal or analysis per SB-1038.
- Use an inspection mirror to check wheel hub and inner surfaces not visible directly. Document any surface anomalies in the maintenance log.

Blast wheel liner bolt torque verification
- With the wheel immobilized and lockout verified, clean the threads and bolt heads of the blast wheel liner fasteners to remove dust and debris that may affect torque readings.
- Using the calibrated torque wrench, apply torque to each blast wheel liner bolt until the wrench indicates the target torque. The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 90 N·m. If any bolt does not achieve the target due to thread damage or slippage, replace the affected fastener and re-torque.
- Sequence torquing in a star pattern to ensure even clamping where applicable; consult SB-1019 for wheel removal/reinstallation detail when disassembly is required.
- Record the torque verification results in the maintenance log, noting bolt locations and any corrective actions.

Shot media management
- Check media level and condition after cleaning. Top-up media as necessary to maintain consistent blast performance. The shot media top-up interval for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 48 hours. Perform top-up at or before the specified interval during scheduled preventive rounds rather than waiting for visible depletion.
- When adding media, use the dedicated media container and funnel to minimize contamination. Avoid mixing different media grades unless validated by process engineering and documented in SB-1038.
- Collect a representative media sample for periodic analysis per SB-1038 to track degradation and contamination trends. Label and retain samples as directed.

Functional check and restart
- After maintenance tasks, verify that all access panels and guards are secured per SB-1019. Remove lockout/tagout only after all tools and personnel are clear and checks are complete.
- Conduct a controlled startup and observe for abnormal vibration, noise, or leakage. If anomalies occur, shut down and investigate per SOP-P3-L4-02.

Examples and rationale for actions
- Example: If during torque verification a bolt loosens below specification repeatedly after successive checks, suspect thread galling, liner seat distortion, or wheel imbalance. Replace the bolt and evaluate wheel runout per SB-1019 before returning the machine to service.
- Rationale: Regular torque verification at the specified value prevents eccentric loading that increases abrasive wear and reduces fatigue life of the wheel assembly.

Acceptance criteria
- All blast wheel liner bolts meet or exceed the specified torque: blast wheel liner bolt torque for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 90 N·m. No bolt may be below this value at the time of inspection.
- No loose fasteners, cracks, or foreign objects remain in the wheel housing after cleaning and inspection.
- Shot media has been topped up within the prescribed period: shot media top-up interval for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 48 hours. Records show top-up actions were performed within this interval.
- No abnormal vibration or noise observed during functional check that would suggest imbalance or misassembly.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry for each visit including date/time, technician name, tasks performed, torque readings for each bolt, media top-up amount (qualitative note of top-up performed), and any defects found.
- Media sample identification and retention record per SB-1038.
- Copy of any corrective actions and parts replaced filed with the equipment history and referenced to SB-1019 when wheel removal or reinstallation was required.
- All records must refer to EQ-P3-L4-SB03 and be retained per plant documentation retention practice and reviewed during periodic audits.

References
- SB-1019
- SB-1038
- SOP-P3-L4-02
